prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: מערכת שעות כיתת י'2 – סמסטר א' (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes.
Merged cells: "ראשון" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שני" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שלישי" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "יום" · longest unbreakable unit 41px · widest one-line content 41px
  col 2: header "שעה" · longest unbreakable unit 48px · widest one-line content 89px
  col 3: header "מקצוע" · longest unbreakable unit 63px · widest one-line content 63px
  col 4: header "מורה" · longest unbreakable unit 42px · widest one-line content 68px
  col 5: header "חדר" · longest unbreakable unit 46px · widest one-line content 76px
  col 6: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable unit 64px · widest one-line content 700px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 720px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 720px wide (column widths sum to at most 719px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 720px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"A weekly class timetable for semester A, organized by day and lesson.","tasks":["Find a lesson by day and time.","Identify its subject, teacher and room.","Read any instructions or changes in the notes."],"relations":["Each lesson row connects a time, subject, teacher, room and note.","Merged day labels group consecutive lessons on the same day.","Notes qualify individual lessons and can contain several instructions."],"roles":["The day column provides grouped row labels; the time column identifies each lesson within a day.","Subject, teacher and room are compact lookup fields.","The notes column carries variable-length prose.","Column headers identify each field and should remain easy to scan."],"keep_whole":["Day names, subject names and column headers.","Each time range, including both endpoints and the dash.","Individual words, room numbers and identifiers."],"may_wrap":["Notes may wrap at natural word boundaries.","Teacher names and multiword room names may wrap between words if needed."],"same_scale":["Day, subject, teacher and room are short lookup fields, though their widths should reflect their content.","Time ranges need a consistent, uninterrupted measure; notes need substantially more space than the lookup fields."],"h_vs_v":"Using the full viewport gives the long notes more room and reduces row height. A narrower table can make the lookup fields more compact, but increases wrapping and makes the timetable taller; merged day labels remain associated with all rows in their groups."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d3r2A, d3r1A.
Measured facts:
d3r2A: column widths [62, 110, 84, 89, 67, 307] px · table 720×477 px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)
d3r1A: column widths [62, 110, 84, 89, 77, 297] px · table 720×500 px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60, 60, 83, 60, 83] · column headers on >1 line: 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 720 px viewport (no scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). Then either propose up to 3 improved designs (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or try an important unexplored idea) or, if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement, set "done": true. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
